title: राष्ट्रपति मुर्मु का मिजोरम और नागालैंड का दौरा, विश्वविद्यालय के दीक्षांत समारोह और हॉर्नबिल महोत्सव में होंगी शामिल - IANS LIVE
search_term: लू (Aizawl OR Champhai OR Kolasib OR Lawngtlai OR Lunglei OR Mamit OR Saiha OR Serchhip) Mizoram
full_text:
आइजोल/कोहिमा, 28 नवंबर (आईएएनएस)। राष्ट्रपति द्रौपदी मुर्मु शनिवार को मिजोरम की तीन दिवसीय यात्रा पर आइजोल पहुंचेंगी। अपनी इस यात्रा के दौरान, वह मिजोरम विश्वविद्यालय (एमजेडयू) के 21वें दीक्षांत समारोह में शामिल होंगी और हाल ही में स्थापित 'रोपुलियानी ट्राइबल फ्रीडम फाइटर्स म्यूजियम' का दौरा करेंगी।
आइजोल के अधिकारियों के अनुसार, राष्ट्रपति रविवार को मिजोरम की राजधानी के पास केल्सिह में 'रोपुलियानी जनजातीय स्वतंत्रता सेनानी संग्रहालय' का दौरा करेंगी।
सोमवार को वह आइजोल के पश्चिमी बाहरी इलाके तानहरिल में मिजोरम विश्वविद्यालय के 21वें दीक्षांत समारोह और विश्वविद्यालय के रजत जयंती समारोह के समापन कार्यक्रम में भी शामिल होंगी।
यह संग्रहालय 'रोपुलियानी' के नाम पर रखा गया है, जो मिजो समुदाय की एक प्रमुख महिला मुखिया और शुरुआती जनजातीय नेता थीं। उन्होंने तत्कालीन लुशाई हिल्स में ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन का विरोध किया था। इस संग्रहालय का उद्घाटन प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने 15 नवंबर को 'जनजातीय गौरव दिवस' के अवसर पर वर्चुअली किया था।
औपनिवेशिक शासन का विरोध करने के कारण अंग्रेजों ने रोपुलियानी को गिरफ्तार कर लिया था और बाद में उन्हें जेल में डाल दिया गया। इसके बाद उन्हें चटगांव हिल ट्रैक्ट्स (अब बांग्लादेश में है) के रंगमती ले जाया गया, जहां जनवरी 1895 में कैद के दौरान ही उनका निधन हो गया।
यह संग्रहालय आइजोल जिले के ऐबॉक ब्लॉक के एक गांव, केल्सिह में स्थित 'जनजातीय अनुसंधान संस्थान' (ट्राइबल रिसर्च इंस्टीट्यूट) में स्थापित किया गया है। यह गांव अब एक पर्यटन और मनोरंजन स्थल के रूप में भी उभर रहा है।
मिजोरम सरकार के एक आधिकारिक बयान के अनुसार, इसके परिसर में एक संग्रहालय भवन, ओपन एयर थिएटर, पारंपरिक झोपड़ी, हेरिटेज वॉक, 'बिरसा मुंडा जनजातीय गौरव उद्यान', कैफेटेरिया और स्टाफ क्वार्टर जैसी कई सुविधाएं मौजूद हैं।
इस परियोजना को केंद्रीय जनजातीय कार्य मंत्रालय द्वारा विकसित किया गया है। इसका उद्देश्य भारत की स्वतंत्रता की लड़ाई में जनजातीय स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों के योगदान और बलिदानों को याद करना और स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन में उनकी भूमिका को उजागर करना है।
एक वरिष्ठ अधिकारी ने बताया कि मंत्रालय ने केल्सिह में इस संग्रहालय की स्थापना के लिए 25.59 करोड़ रुपए की मंजूरी दी थी।
केंद्रीय जनजातीय कार्य मंत्रालय 10 राज्यों में 11 'जनजातीय स्वतंत्रता सेनानी संग्रहालय' स्थापित कर रहा है। इनका उद्देश्य ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के खिलाफ हुए जनजातीय आंदोलनों और विद्रोहों को याद करना, और जनजातीय समुदायों की समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक विरासत, इतिहास, परंपराओं और उनके योगदान को प्रदर्शित करना है।
इन संग्रहालयों का उद्देश्य आदिवासी स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों की विरासत को संरक्षित करना और उसे बढ़ावा देना है, साथ ही भारत के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में उनकी महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका को अधिक पहचान दिलाना है।
मणिपुर के तामेंगलोंग में भी इसी तरह का एक 'आदिवासी स्वतंत्रता सेनानी संग्रहालय' स्थापित किया जा रहा है।
मिजोरम के बाद, राष्ट्रपति मुर्मु नागालैंड जाएंगी। वहां 1 दिसंबर को कोहिमा से लगभग 12 किमी दक्षिण में स्थित किसामा के 'नागा हेरिटेज विलेज' में, वह 27वें 'हॉर्नबिल फेस्टिवल' के उद्घाटन समारोह में शामिल होंगी।
नागालैंड सरकार ने इस वार्षिक सांस्कृतिक उत्सव की तैयारियां शुरू कर दी हैं। यह उत्सव 1 दिसंबर को राज्य के 64वें स्थापना दिवस के मौके पर आयोजित हो रहा है।
10 दिनों तक चलने वाला यह उत्सव 1 से 10 दिसंबर तक आयोजित होगा, जिसमें कई देशों के शामिल होने की उम्मीद है।
नागालैंड के सबसे प्रमुख सांस्कृतिक आयोजनों में से एक, 'हॉर्नबिल फेस्टिवल' में राज्य की विविध आदिवासी परंपराओं, स्थानीय कला, संगीत, नृत्य, खान-पान और समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक विरासत की झलक देखने को मिलती है।

The severe weather system that began moving in from western Greece on Thursday night into Friday is now fully underway. It is progressing slowly eastwards and will affect almost the entire country over the weekend.
According to the emergency severe weather bulletin issued by the Hellenic National Meteorological Service (HNMS), today, Saturday, the Ionian Islands, Epirus and western Central Greece are under a “red” alert. Western Peloponnese has been placed under an “orange” alert, as have parts of Central Macedonia, specifically Pieria and Halkidiki, as well as eastern Thessaly, from Saturday evening onwards.
As far as Attica is concerned, rain is expected today, Saturday, mainly from the afternoon onwards. The HNMS forecast refers to isolated thunderstorms.
According to meteorologist Giorgos Tsatrafyllias, one indication of the severity of the situation is that forecasting models for the red-alert areas suggest that rainfall could amount to “the equivalent of two to three Novembers’ worth of rain by Saturday afternoon”.
Sunday will be the most difficult day
The weather is expected to deteriorate further on Sunday, when the storm front will have moved further east.
According to the HNMS, heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast for tomorrow, Sunday, initially in Thessaly, eastern Central Greece (particularly the regional unit of Phthiotis) and Evia. Eastern and southern Peloponnese will gradually be affected as well.
In Attica in particular, large amounts of rainfall are expected, mainly in the western and northern parts of the region, from midday and throughout the afternoon.
Megara, Elefsina, Mandra, Mount Parnitha, Dionysos and Oropos are among the areas expected to receive the heaviest rainfall in Attica. Cumulative rainfall totals by the end of Sunday could locally exceed even 100 millimetres. (It should be noted that 100 millimetres of rain is equivalent to 100 litres of water per square metre.)
Significant rainfall is also forecast in central Athens, the eastern suburbs and along the coastal zone, as almost the entire region is expected to fall within the area of substantial precipitation.
The estimated cumulative rainfall totals by the end of Sunday are as follows:
- Western Attica (Megara, Elefsina, Mandra): 60–100 millimetres of rain, with the possibility of even higher amounts locally.
- Northern Attica (Mount Parnitha, Dionysos, Oropos): 70–100 millimetres, with the possibility that these figures will be exceeded in mountainous areas.
- Central Athens: 40–70 millimetres.
- Eastern Attica (Gerakas, Pallini, Rafina, Marathon): 50–80 millimetres.
- Southern suburbs and coastal zone: 40–70 millimetres.
Strong winds and falling temperatures
In addition to the rain, Sunday’s weather will be characterised by very strong northerly to northeasterly winds, reaching force 9 on the Beaufort scale and locally force 10 in the Aegean. Gusts are expected to reach up to 120 km/h in the northern Aegean and 90 km/h in Attica.
The winds are also expected to bring a drop in temperature of up to 10 degrees Celsius.
Emergency measures to protect workers during Saturday’s severe weather: What the circular provides for
The Ministry of Labour has issued a circular introducing emergency measures to protect private-sector workers in view of the extreme weather conditions expected across a large part of the country on Saturday, November 28.
The circular provides for the mandatory suspension of outdoor work, the provision of remote working arrangements and measures to facilitate employees’ arrival at and departure from work.
The text of the circular
A. Mandatory suspension of outdoor work
For employees of businesses operating in areas where extreme weather conditions are expected, according to the updated Emergency Severe Weather Bulletin (ESWB) issued by the National Meteorological Service, the suspension of work is mandatory throughout Saturday, November 28, 2026, in particular in the Region of Western Greece, the Regional Unit of the Ionian Islands and the Regional Unit of Epirus.
The measure applies to manual work carried out outdoors, such as work on technical and construction projects, building sites, shipbuilding and ship-repair zones, and the delivery and transportation of products and items using two-wheeled vehicles, scooters or roller skates (delivery services), among other activities.
It is noted that the above cases of mandatory work suspension cover all employees, regardless of their type of employment, including workers operating through digital platforms under Article 68 of Law 4808/2021.
The suspension of work does not apply to economic activities involving important and socially critical infrastructure in the fields of health, transport and public utilities (for example, healthcare facilities, water supply, electricity, air transport, ground handling, maritime, road and rail transport), provided that the necessary measures are taken to protect employees’ health and safety. These include the provision of appropriate personal protective equipment, in accordance with current legislation.
In the event of non-compliance with the obligations set out in this circular, the Labour Inspectorate will impose a fine of two thousand (€2,000) euros for each employee of the business, pursuant to Articles 23 and 24 of Law 3996/2011 (Government Gazette A’ 170).
B. Provision of remote work through teleworking arrangements
In order to protect workers in areas expected to be particularly affected, according to the updated Emergency Severe Weather Bulletin issued by the National Meteorological Service, the Ministry of Labour and Social Security recommends that private-sector businesses implement remote working wherever this is organisationally feasible.
C. Emergency measures concerning the organisation of working hours
For the purposes of implementing this circular and facilitating employees in the event that their arrival and departure times need to be changed, employers in areas expected to be particularly affected, according to the updated Emergency Severe Weather Bulletin issued by the National Meteorological Service, may refrain from registering in advance any changes to working-time arrangements in the ERGANI Information System.

November 27, 2026 Hour: 7:11 pm
Panama is under a heat alert this Friday, with temperatures reaching 36 degrees Celsius and a heat index of up to 42 degrees, prompting authorities to urge hydration, light clothing, and reduced sun exposure.
The Institute of Meteorology and Hydrology of Panama (IMHPA) issued the alert, which remains in force through Monday, November 30. “Over the course of the day, conditions may reach the ‘danger’ category, increasing the likelihood of sunstroke, cramps, and heat stroke due to prolonged sun exposure or intense physical activity,” the agency said.
The heat index measures how hot the body perceives conditions to be, based on a combination of weather parameters, including elevated humidity. In Panama, daytime highs are expected to range between 32 and 36 degrees Celsius, with relative humidity near 80 percent. Together, those factors generate a perceived temperature of 35 to 42 degrees.
RELATED: Extreme Heat in 2023-2024 Drove Unprecedented Global Freshwater Decline
That combination pushes the body harder than the thermometer alone would suggest. High humidity slows the evaporation of sweat, the body’s natural cooling mechanism, and turns an already warm afternoon into a health hazard for anyone exposed without protection.
Panama has a predominantly tropical climate, with average temperatures that generally vary between 24 and 32 degrees Celsius. The country now sits in transition between the rainy season, which begins in May, and the dry season, which starts in December and typically runs through April.
Text reads: “Warning of Surveillance for Elevated Temperature and Thermal Sensation. Continuing the mostly dry and warm environment over the Pacific sector of the Panamanian isthmus, high thermal sensation is expected from early morning between 35°C and 42°C.”
El Niño Drives Drought
Specialists recalled that Panama’s tropical climate has been altered throughout 2026 by the presence of the El Niño phenomenon. The event drives severe drought across Central America, and official records show it has remained active for five consecutive months.
This year, the rainy season has been altered by the El Niño phenomenon, which produces severe droughts across Central America. The event has remained active for five consecutive months and is expected to continue, according to the Panamanian meteorological institute.
El Niño warms surface waters in the tropical Pacific, disrupting weather patterns far beyond the ocean itself. For Panama and its neighbors, the consequence is drier conditions that amplify heat already typical of the dry season. Forecasters expect the phenomenon to keep influencing regional atmospheric conditions.
The alert arrives as the country also manages the aftermath of a recent earthquake. For Panamanian authorities, the coming days will test whether public guidance can hold back a predictable surge in heat-related illness. With temperatures expected to remain elevated through Monday and El Niño lingering over the region, the alert marks the start of a longer season of risk rather than a passing spike.
The meteorological institute warned that prolonged exposure to solar radiation or intense physical activity increases the risk of sunstroke, cramps, and heat stroke. The danger is not limited to a single hour of the day but stretches across the afternoon, when temperatures and humidity combine most aggressively.
The measures now in place focus on prevention. Hydration, shade, and rest during peak hours are the main defenses against conditions that escalate quickly from discomfort to medical emergency. Whether those precautions reach the most vulnerable households will determine how the country weathers the heat still ahead.
With El Niño expected to keep influencing regional conditions, the current alert may be an early sign of a longer dry season ahead. For Panamanian authorities, the challenge is not just managing this week’s heat but preparing communities for months of elevated risk.

By Nkiruka Nnorom
The United Nations has urged Nigeria to treat the early warning signs of electoral violence already emerging ahead of the 2027 general elections as a call to action, warning that prevention must come before election day.
The call was made at the 2027 Elections Stakeholders Conference at the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA) by Ms. Grace Kpohazounde, Senior Peace and Development Advisor, United Nations Resident Coordinator’s Office, Nigeria, who joined virtually.
The Conference with the theme: “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Security Threats and Pathways to National Stability”, was organised by NIIA’s The General LEO Irabor Early Warning Centre and supported by FirstHoldco Plc.
Speaking, Kpohazounde said elections in Nigeria have unfortunately become a period when security becomes a concern and tensions are exploited, adding that the conversation on election security must shift to prevention as a priority.
She said: “As we look towards 2027, I want to flag that talking about election security should be a conversation that we try to address ahead of elections, making a point of prevention as a priority when it comes to discussing electoral security.
“While we have had positive experiences this year in terms of off-cycle elections, there were lessons learned. We continue to have early warning signs in terms of electoral violence and electoral incidents and these should be treated as early warning signs that need to be addressed before election days.”
She said the protection of political participation and the prevention of electoral violence must go together, noting that inclusive processes reinforce legitimacy and strengthen public confidence in elections.
She warned that exclusion breeds violence, saying: “Exclusion can lead to some militants and also some stakeholders choosing the voice of violence when they feel that their voices are not being heard. So ensuring an inclusive process is key to also making sure that everyone feels recognized and that their voices are heard, that violence is not really an avenue to communicate one’s interests in an electoral process.”
She disclosed that although the UN does not have a specific mandate to provide electoral assistance this time, it remains committed and engaged in Nigeria.
She stressed that the 2027 elections are important not only for Nigeria but for the entire West Africa region, because countries look up to Nigeria and its democratic processes.
According to her, ensuring success in 2027 is a shared responsibility of government institutions, political parties and candidates, security agencies, civil society and the media and charged the media to communicate information accurately and avoid distortions that could incite violence.
Corroborating the UN position, Mr. Serigne Ka, Head, Electoral Assistance Division, ECOWAS Commission charged all political actors and stakeholders in Nigeria to demonstrate restraint, uphold democratic principles, and refrain from inflammatory rhetoric, intimidation and actions capable of undermining public confidence in the 2027 general elections.
Ka, who spoke on behalf of Dr. Babatunde Afolabi, Director of Political Affairs, said the call followed the findings of the ECOWAS pre-election fact-finding mission to Nigeria, led by former Vice President Dr. Victor Bokarifu, which assessed the country’s level of preparedness for the 2027 polls.
He said the mission noted remarkable progress in strengthening the electoral framework and institutional preparedness, but identified electoral security as the major outstanding concern.
“It is the business of everybody, for everybody, all political actors, all political stakeholders, to demonstrate restraint, to uphold democratic principles, and especially to refrain from inflammatory rhetoric, intimidation, and actions that may undermine public confidence in the electoral process.
“The mission made a particular recommendation to security agencies to discharge their responsibilities professionally, to show impartiality, and to work in accordance with the law,” he said.
Ka said priority must be accorded to preventing electoral violence, noting that Nigeria is not only the biggest country in West Africa, but also the strongest, and occupies a very strategic position in the political, economic and security architecture of the community.
He warned that developments surrounding Nigeria’s electoral process have implications that extend beyond its national borders, citing the events in Benin on December 5, 2025 as an example of how instability can spread in the sub-region.
He disclosed that ECOWAS would deploy a sizable, special mission to Nigeria beyond its routine observer missions to focus on preventive diplomacy and consolidating the security environment, to stop tensions from escalating into political instability or violence.
He said the deployment would reaffirm ECOWAS’ institutional commitment to constitutional convergence, democratic accountability and peaceful political transition.
Ptof. Eghosa Osaghae, Director General of NIIA, said its Stakeholders Conference on the 2027 elections is part of Nigeria’s early warning architecture to detect and prevent electoral violence before it escalates.
He said the Institute identified early warning in the electoral sector as a major gap in Nigeria’s security system, and decided to fill it through its Early Warning Systems Centre.
He said the conference was organised to examine security threats and unwanted signals ahead of the elections, and to ensure the country is fully prepared.
He said: “This is part of our early warning architecture. When the Early Warning Systems Centre was being set up, we were looking for ways that would serve as cutting edge for the kind of work we are doing.
“We have seen early warning systems in several places and we identified early warning in the electoral sector as one of the gaps that we haven’t covered properly. So, this is part of the contribution that that centre is making to ensuring that we have a process that we are fully prepared for.”
The DG lamented that electoral violence and electoral instability have become part and parcel of what Nigerians expect any time elections are held, with the country preparing for elections as though preparing for war.
He said: “People always ask the question, why do we prepare for elections as though we’re preparing for war? Elections are not wars, even though we have winners and losers but winners and losers of a civil kind, not of a violent kind.”
He said one of the indices of electoral success would be voter turnout, and called for efforts to make voting a pleasurable event that Nigerians look forward to, rather than a ritual they fear.
Mike Igini, former Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) warned that Nigeria must not allow the 2027 general elections to fail, saying failed elections in other African countries have left populations homeless, hopeless and forced into migration.
He said election is the heartbeat of democracy and a promise that the will of the people will form the government, but said that promise can only hold if citizens are able to vote in a safe environment and have their votes counted.
“We have seen in places across Africa, where failed elections led to people becoming homeless, hopeless, discontented and tired, and forced into migration on account of failed elections.
That should not happen in our country. We have a duty to ensure it does not happen,” he said.
Igini stressed that election season remains the most dangerous season in Nigeria’s national life, warning that violence has no place in democracy because it destroys participation and accountability.
Igini also warned that with hunger in the land, any attempt by individuals or groups to deny Nigerians their franchise in 2027 would be dangerous.
He called on Nigerians, security agencies, and the international community, including the United States and the European Union, to pay close attention to the pre-election period, which he described as critical to the success of the election.
